# #709 — pr-body-gate never sets PR_HEAD_REF, so #706's branch-resolution tier is unreachable from the only caller that runs

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy

## What happens

The #706 fix landed in two halves and only one of them is reachable in
production.

`scripts/validate-pr-body.ts` resolves a `Done-means` path in three tiers —
the tree under review (`PR_REPO_DIR`), the validator's own tree, and
`git cat-file -e <PR_HEAD_REF>:<path>` against the head branch
(`validate-pr-body.ts:331-337`). The third tier is the one #706 asked for by
name: it is what lets a lane cite a check that exists only on its own branch.

`.claude/hooks/pr-body-gate.ts` — the only caller that runs at the boundary —
sets `PR_REPO_DIR` (`pr-body-gate.ts:356`) and **never sets `PR_HEAD_REF`**.
It also parses no `--head` flag from the `gh pr create` command line
(`rg -n 'head' .claude/hooks/pr-body-gate.ts` matches only prose in comments).
So the branch tier is unreachable from the hook, and the fix reduces to
"resolve against `input.cwd`".

That would still work if `input.cwd` were the lane worktree. It is not.
`input.cwd` is the harness payload's cwd — the SESSION's directory — and a
`cd /path/to/worktree && gh pr create ...` inside a single Bash call does not
change it. The hook's own comment states the intended source correctly ("the
tree the command was actually run from — the lane worktree"), but the payload
does not carry that.

## Measured 2026-08-10, lane `lane/issue-artifacts-outcomes` (rebased at `134b0b8`)

Creating the PR from the lane worktree, with the check committed and pushed on
the branch, is refused — and the refusal names the primary checkout as the only
tree it looked in:

```
BLOCKED by pr-body-gate: this PR body fails scripts/validate-pr-body.ts.
- Verification field 'Done-means' must name an existing repo-relative path;
  not found: scripts/done-means/issue-resolution-artifacts.sh
  (looked in: /Volumes/ThunderBolt/Development/open-brain)
```

The same body, same validator, same primary checkout, with `PR_HEAD_REF`
supplied by hand, passes — and announces the branch tier exactly as designed:

```
PR_BODY="$(cat prbody.md)" PR_TITLE="..." \
  PR_HEAD_REF="lane/issue-artifacts-outcomes" bun scripts/validate-pr-body.ts
# => Done-means resolved in branch lane/issue-artifacts-outcomes
#    (/Volumes/ThunderBolt/Development/open-brain), not on disk in any available tree
# => PR body validation passed.   EXIT=0
```

So the validator half is correct and proven. The hook half does not deliver the
input the validator needs.

## Why the done-means checks did not catch it

`scripts/done-means/706-done-means-resolves-pr-head.sh` is 5/5 GREEN against
this same tree. It tests the VALIDATOR directly and sets `PR_HEAD_REF` itself,
so it proves the tier works when fed — never that anything feeds it.
`scripts/done-means/pr-body-gate-fires.sh` exercises the hook but asserts on
neither `cwd` nor `PR_HEAD_REF` (`rg -n 'PR_HEAD_REF|cwd'` returns nothing).

This is `docs/lane-contract.md` round 28's own first bullet recurring in the
lane that wrote it: **a seam added to make a gate testable is not the path that
runs.** The convenience entry point (call the validator directly) passed while
the real invocation shape (the hook, with a harness payload) failed.

## Suggested direction (not implemented here)

Have the hook supply the head ref rather than inferring the tree:

1. Parse `--head` from the intercepted `gh pr create` argv when present.
2. Otherwise resolve the current branch of the tree the command targets.
3. Pass it as `PR_HEAD_REF`, and keep `PR_REPO_DIR` as-is — the tiers are
   complementary, not alternatives.
4. Add a clause to `pr-body-gate-fires.sh` that drives the HOOK with a payload
   whose `cwd` is NOT the branch's tree, and asserts a branch-only path is
   accepted. That is the clause whose absence let this ship.

Keep the refusal's "looked in:" list, and extend it to name the ref that was
probed, so a future refusal says which tiers actually ran.

## Discussion (1)

### rodaddy — 2026-08-10T02:15:19Z

Fixed and MERGED to `wip/2026-08-07` as `6e3198f` (PR #713, squash of `5031f0a`).

## What changed

`.claude/hooks/pr-body-gate.ts` now tells the validator what the PR actually
is, in a fixed precedence, and announces which source answered:

1. `--head`/`-H` parsed from the intercepted `gh pr create` (was not parsed at
   all before).
2. else the branch checked out in the directory the command `cd`s into — the
   `cd <worktree> && gh pr create` shape this issue measured.
3. else the payload cwd.

`PR_REPO_DIR` follows the same target directory, so the tree tier and the
branch tier stay complementary rather than alternatives, exactly as this issue
asked. Both inputs are now printed on the REFUSAL path too, which is the thing
that made this defect expensive to diagnose: the original refusal named the
tree it searched but not where that tree came from, so it read as "your path
does not exist" when the truth was "the gate looked in the wrong place".

Every step degrades to the pre-fix behaviour rather than guessing — a `cd -`, a
variable-built path, or a detached HEAD yields no hint. `branchOf` uses
`symbolic-ref --quiet --short` rather than `rev-parse`, because a raw SHA is a
valid `git cat-file` argument and would have produced the announcement
"resolved in branch 9f3a1c2" — a non-fact in the grammar of a fact.

## Verified on the integration branch

```
$ git cat-file -e origin/wip/2026-08-07:scripts/done-means/709-hook-feeds-head-ref.sh
$ git show origin/wip/2026-08-07:.claude/hooks/pr-body-gate.ts | rg -c PR_HEAD_REF
3
```

## The done-means answers this issue's "Why the checks did not catch it"

`scripts/done-means/709-hook-feeds-head-ref.sh` drives the REAL hook entry with
synthetic PreToolUse payloads whose `cwd` is not the branch's tree. No
validator-direct seam is used as proof anywhere in it — that was the specific
mistake. RED 4/5 before the fix, GREEN 5/5 after, with clause 4 as a mutant
control passing on both sides (a path in no tree and on no ref stays refused,
so widening resolution did not become a blanket pass).

Clause 2 is the one this issue's third suggestion asks for: it moves the check
out of the lane worktree while it stays committed on the branch, so no
reachable checkout carries it and ONLY a supplied `PR_HEAD_REF` can answer. A
fix that merely read the `cd` target passes clause 1 and still fails clause 2 —
which is how #706 shipped half-done.

Re-run 5/5 GREEN in an independent `verify-lane` worktree; the receipt bound to
`5031f0a` is on PR #713.

## Bootstrap ordering, declared

PR #713 could not cite its own new check, because the registered hook is
`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/pr-body-gate.ts` — the primary checkout's
unfixed copy. So it cited `pr-body-gate-fires.sh` (the standing acceptance test
for the very hook being modified, present on the base branch, 8/8 GREEN), and
printed both the refusing OLD-hook run and the accepting FIXED-hook run in the
body. No `--no-verify`, no bypass. Now that this is merged the next lane can
cite its own check directly — which is the whole point of the issue.
